network_findings: Colorado contractor licensing is specialty-based statewide for electrical and plumbing. There is no statewide general-contractor license universe. General contractors remain primarily a local licensing model.
Colorado has a genuine PUC household-goods permit layer that is separate from FMCSA interstate authority. A state HHG permit is not a USDOT number and not MC authority.
Senior evidence is strongest when CMS nursing homes, home health, and hospice stay separate classes and CDPHE adds state verification context. Do not publish one Colorado senior-providers total.
Lender has strong MLO person-license and 2025 HMDA property-location intelligence, but no acquired current bulk mortgage-company roster. HMDA is not a license. An MLO is not a lender company.

Investor has an unusually strong state-registration layer because official IAPD state compilation exposes jurisdiction-based IA and ERA records. 740 approved state IA firms are not 589 principal-office firms and not 3,673 notice filings.

Insurance has strong DOI market, surplus-lines, and complaint evidence despite missing free agency, producer, and current-authorized bulk rosters. 1,839 statistical-directory rows are not current authorization. DOI Complaint Ratio/Index is not a TrustHub score.
conceptual_statement: Colorado’s strongest Trust Hub evidence is specialty contractor credentials (not a statewide general-contractor license), a genuine PUC household-goods permit layer, separate CMS senior provider classes with CDPHE verification context, HMDA mortgage-market activity with a search-only company roster, an unusually strong IAPD state-registration layer for investment advisers, and DOI market, surplus-lines, and complaint evidence that is not a live authorized-insurer roster. Organizations and evidence records stay separate. Missing, restricted, and search-only sources are unknown — not zero.
